clue.text: Estonian at sea rounds area with good wind up

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so the nationality's letters are thrown into disorder
to round something is to go all the way about it, so the jumbled word encloses what follows

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
A for area and G for good, two standard abbreviations

explanation.surface: A seasick Estonian sailor circles a patch of sea with a fair breeze behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' reads as a nautical breeze, fitting 'at sea', but it is the definition: British slang for annoying someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up is British slang for deliberately irritating or provoking them, which is to antagonise them.

clue.text: Second-rate physician screening old engineers

indicators.note: a screen hides something behind or within it, so the doctor's word wraps around the next letter

blocks.note: a medic is a doctor
O is the standard abbreviation for old
the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A poor doctor examining some elderly engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a corps of the British Army, a standard crossword source for two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre is only ordinary or below average quality, exactly what second-rate describes.

clue.text: A father filled with quiet hope

indicators.note: a vessel filled with something holds it inside, so the parent's word takes in the musical letter

blocks.note: taken as written
to sire is to father, and a sire is a male parent
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A dad brimming with silent longing.
explanation.walkthrough: Quiet is p because piano is the musical marking for playing softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to long or aim for something, which as a verb is close to wishing or hoping for it.

clue.text: What might prevent IT boss getting hurt

blocks.note: a head is the person in charge
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: An office scene: the head of the IT department is injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT boss' looks like the head of computing, but 'IT' belongs to the definition: it is the coy euphemism for sex, and a headache is the classic excuse for avoiding it.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock excuse 'not tonight, I have a headache' is the traditional way of declining intimacy, so it can stop sex happening.

clue.text: One spotted falling over themselves in a run?

definitions.text: One spotted falling over themselves in a run?

blocks.clueFragment: One spotted falling over themselves in a run?
blocks.note: surface reading: a clumsy spotty person, perhaps a dalmatian, tumbling over during a race

blocks.clueFragment: One spotted falling over themselves in a run?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a tile marked with pips that topples in a line of identical tiles, each knocking over the next

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' suggests a race, but here it is a row of upright tiles; 'themselves' hints that every one in the line falls the same way, as in the famous chain-reaction effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of this game are marked with spots, and stood in a row they fall one after another when the first is pushed.

clue.text: Suitors essentially regret being faithful

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the very centre of the word is wanted

blocks.note: the central letter of this seven-letter word
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Wooers, at heart, are sorry for having stayed loyal.
explanation.definitionFit: A true friend or lover is a loyal one, so the adjective matches faithful in the sense of steadfast devotion.

clue.text: Stake or pole stuck in unopened turnstile?

indicators.note: something unopened has had its opening taken away, so the first letter of the word goes
a thing stuck in another sits inside it, so the compass letter goes inside the shortened word

blocks.note: a turnstile is an example of a gate, hence the question mark
N for north, one of the Earth's poles

explanation.surface: A post or stake jammed in a turnstile that won't open.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a turnstile is only one kind of gate, a definition by example inside the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker an ante is the stake each player puts into the pot before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: What one on deck will do with fish food

definitions.text: What one on deck will do

blocks.note: a skate is a flat fish related to the ray
board means meals, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck deciding what to do with the fish rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On deck' suggests a ship, but a deck is also the flat board of a skateboard; the answer is the verb for riding one.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat platform a rider stands on is called the deck, so someone on one will ride it, which is the verb sense.

clue.text: Where one’s comfortably in even though one’s out?

definitions.text: Where one’s comfortably in even though one’s out?

blocks.clueFragment: Where one’s comfortably in even though one’s out?
blocks.note: surface reading: a paradox, being both inside and outside at once

blocks.clueFragment: Where one’s comfortably in even though one’s out?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a place away from where one lives that feels just as cosy as one's own house

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' means staying in, at one's own dwelling, and 'out' means away from it; the phrase describes somewhere that makes being away feel like being there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a place, such as a friend's house or favourite hotel, where you feel as relaxed as in your own dwelling.

clue.text: Pot that’s hot given to one for a snack

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking pot
hot and in both mean fashionable
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hot pan is handed to someone to make a quick bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' seems to describe the pot's temperature, but it is the fashionable sense, IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Panini are toasted Italian sandwiches, commonly eaten as a light snack.

clue.text: Senior around uni needing to retire, say

definitions.text: Senior around uni needing to retire, say

indicators.note: the first word goes around the outside of what follows, enclosing it
to retire is to draw back, so the university's letters run backwards

blocks.note: senior means older in age
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, a university

explanation.surface: An elderly academic at a university who ought to be retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The whole clue also describes one example of the answer, a long-serving don due to retire, flagged by 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is a veteran who has been around a long time, and an aged professor due for retirement is one example.

clue.text: Prisoner on Greek island gets physical

indicators.note: in an across clue one part sits on another by coming right before it

blocks.note: a con is a convict
the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: An inmate on a Greek island turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets physical' reads as a phrase meaning becoming rough, but 'gets' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete means real and tangible, existing in material form, which is the solid sense of physical.

clue.text: Dope, heroin and ecstasy habit

blocks.note: a clot is a fool, as is a dope
H is slang for heroin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A list of drugs forming an addiction: dope, heroin and ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: With drugs everywhere, 'Dope' and 'habit' suggest addiction; here dope is a fool and habit is a verb, to dress, as in a habited nun.
explanation.definitionFit: To habit someone is an old verb meaning to dress them, as monks and nuns are habited in their robes.

clue.text: Ethics don I led astray purely for fun

indicators.note: something led astray wanders off its proper course, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An ethics lecturer confesses he has misled people just for amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonism is the pursuit of pleasure, so a hedonistic act is done simply for enjoyment.

clue.text: New index nice peer muddled up

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so these words' letters are mixed into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh index has a kindly lord confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective for the index, but it is the definition in the sense of a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone new to a job or activity lacks practice and knowledge, so is green or untried.

clue.text: Organisation looking for gold outside of Lima

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so the prospecting word wraps the phonetic letter

blocks.note: panning is sifting river gravel in a pan to find gold
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A company prospecting for gold beyond the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like Peru's capital, a natural site for gold prospecting, but it is the radio code word for L.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning is the arranging and coordinating of things in advance, which is organisation in the sense of preparation.

clue.text: Cabinet committee to support Catholic on trial

indicators.note: in a down clue a support sits underneath, so the committee word comes below the rest

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Catholic
to be up before a court is to be on trial
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A government committee backs a Catholic who is facing trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet committee' reads as a government body, but Cabinet is the definition, a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is a piece of furniture with shelves and doors for storage, exactly what a cabinet is.

clue.text: A former state or a former state without mass

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the abbreviation for mass is taken away from the old kingdom's name

blocks.note: a as in 'five pounds a head', meaning per
the old name of Thailand
m is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A riddle about history: name an old country, or another old country with something missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter repeats 'former state' on purpose: the repetition tempts a double definition, but the second half is wordplay, with 'a' meaning per, as in 'a pound a head', and Thailand's old name losing its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the name of the country now called Iran until 1935, so it is a historical nation.

clue.text: Sad about Britain? Just a little!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the small-quantity word goes round the country's abbreviation

blocks.note: some means a small amount
BR is an abbreviation for Britain

explanation.surface: Are you sad about the state of Britain? Only slightly!
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means dark and gloomy in mood, so it describes someone melancholy or downcast.

clue.text: Mess with pint spilt? Must be wasted!

indicators.note: spilt liquid is scattered everywhere, so the letters are splashed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spilt pint makes a mess, and the beer has gone to waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Misspent money or time has been used foolishly or squandered, as in a misspent youth.

clue.text: Old city district in South Africa

indicators.note: one thing sits in another, so the region word goes inside the country's abbreviation

blocks.note: a part is an area or district, as in 'this part of town'
SA is the standard abbreviation for South Africa

explanation.surface: An ancient urban area located in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece, famous for its military discipline.

clue.text: Leggy type seen in red-hot video ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: flaming means burning, red-hot
the last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A long-legged model appears in a steamy music video.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the bird is pink-red, so 'red-hot' doubles as a hint to its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamingos are wading birds with very long thin legs, so the playful description fits them.

clue.text: Sumptuous boozer

blocks.note: first meaning: rich, luxurious
second meaning: a heavy drinker

explanation.walkthrough: In British English a boozer is also a pub, which tempts a solver; here it is the drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means luxurious and opulent, while the noun is slang for an alcoholic or heavy drinker.

clue.text: To get going, a Dodge needs oxygen injection

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the gas symbol goes into the trick word

blocks.note: taken as written
a dodge is a trick or ruse
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: To start up, a Dodge car engine needs an oxygen boost.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodge, capitalised, looks like the car make, but it means a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse is to stir or awaken someone or something into activity, to get them moving.

clue.text: Caustic row in a department of the NHS

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it, so the line word goes within the hospital department

blocks.note: taken as written
a string is a row or line, as in a string of pearls
the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital; the NHS is Britain's National Health Service

explanation.surface: A bitter argument breaks out in a British hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, fitting 'caustic', but it is a line, as in a string of beads.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are sharp and severe, the same biting harshness as caustic comments.

clue.text: One breaking ladder causes havoc

indicators.note: something breaking into another gets inside it, so the numeral goes within the tights word

blocks.note: in British English a ladder is a run in tights or stockings
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A broken rung on a ladder leads to chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder in British usage is a run in tights, not something to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin as a noun means devastation or destruction, the same state of chaos as havoc.
